content: 1. Budesonide is indicated for the induction of remission in active, mild-to-moderate ulcerative colitis at a dose of 9 mg orally once daily in the morning for up to 8 weeks. 2. Entocort EC is indicated for the treatment of mild-to-moderate active Crohn's disease involving the ileum and/or ascending colon. 3. Tarpeyo is indicated to reduce the loss of kidney function in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) who are at risk of disease progression. The recommended dose is 16 mg orally once daily for 9 months. When discontinuing, the dose should be reduced to 8 mg orally once daily for the last 2 weeks of therapy. The safety and efficacy of subsequent treatment courses have not been established. 4. Eohilia is indicated for eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) in patients aged 11 years and older. The recommended dose is 2 mg (10 mL) orally twice daily for 12 weeks. 5. Eohilia has an orphan designation for slowing the progression of immunoglobulin A nephropathy and delaying the onset of kidney failure in affected patients. 6. Eohilia also has an orphan designation for the treatment of primary biliary cholangitis. 7. Eohilia has not been shown to be safe and effective for the treatment of EoE for longer than 12 weeks. 8. Entocort EC is indicated for mild-to-moderate active Crohn's disease involving the ileum and/or ascending colon in patients aged 8 years and older. For patients under 8 years of age, safety and efficacy have not been established. For patients aged 8 years and older and weighing more than 25 kg, the recommended dose is 9 mg orally once daily in the morning for up to 8 weeks, followed by 6 mg once daily in the morning for 2 weeks. 9. Budesonide (Uceris) has an orphan designation for the treatment of ulcerative colitis in pediatric patients aged 0 through 16 years. 10. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of budesonide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Mifepristone is contraindicated with budesonide due to an unknown mechanism. The manufacturer states that mifepristone is contraindicated in patients on long-term corticosteroid therapy. 12. Co-administration of apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, with drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates can result in lower exposure to these medications. If co-administration is unavoidable, evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose according to prescribing information. 16.
